task: Google sign-up is broken. Diagnose and fix the root cause without changing working email or OTP authentication, and add the smallest regression check that proves the failure is gone.

diagnosis.baseline: Best quality. Broad search plus Git history recovered both Google signup and login, but at the highest token and dollar cost.
diagnosis.current: Fastest and cheapest. RepoTracer identified the backend and both UI surfaces, but the parent wrote a regression test against a duplicated test fixture rather than production configuration.
diagnosis.variant: The new policy behaved as designed: RepoTracer ran first and the parent performed one targeted Git-history lookup. It then overfit to signup, omitted Google login, and spent more time and tokens than unchanged RepoTracer.
diagnosis.decision: Reject this regression-aware wording. Keep current RepoTracer routing for now; it preserved most of the quality while materially reducing compute. A future change should require checking sibling user-visible entry points and testing the real shared module, not merely invite history lookup.

validation.current_infrastructure_note: After implementation and required checks, the Codex process ended on invalid previous_response_id. The patch and completed checks were still gradeable; no final-answer artifact was emitted.

limitations: One task and one run per arm: diagnostic only, not a general product claim.
Runs were sequential; wall time is sensitive to host and provider load.
Blind graders scored patches after common focused validation, not live browser behavior.
The current arm's terminal provider error may have shortened its run after the required implementation and checks.
